disposition_mapping.rationale: Council consensus (maximalist, pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect) treats due-item selection as a deterministic, rule-evaluable filter already largely system-mediated today ('AP analyst with ERP'). It merges with PRE-02 into one automated step, but the mandatory input 'Approved matched invoices' (PRE-R-01) is preserved explicitly, and the human role persists, narrowed to owning an exception queue for disputed, stale-master-data, or volatile-FX items rather than vanishing — satisfying emerging_economy's and hitl_designer's insistence that mechanical automation not silently absorb anomalous items.

Unanimous council view that vendor/currency/payment-method grouping is mechanical aggregation with no independent judgment boundary from PRE-01. Merged into TGT-01; PRE-R-08 (survival) is satisfied because the proposal-generation function and artifact persist, with accounting_standards' concern (currency grouping is the precondition for correct FX handling, KB-08) preserved as explicit grouping logic inside the agent.

Near-unanimous agreement (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards) that this is the workflow's primary fraud/error control (duplicate payment, blocked vendor, bank-detail-change — KB-05, KB-11) and must not be reduced to a rubber stamp or eliminated. Resolved in favour of automating detection (100%-of-line screening) while keeping a human AP-supervisor disposition on every flag, plus a residual random sample of unflagged lines (hitl_designer's and agentic_architect's shared refinement) to guard against screening-tool blind spots — rejecting maximalist's pure exception-only design as insufficiently defended against false negatives.

This is the council's central resolved conflict. Six of seven members (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, accounting_standards-as-neutral-arbiter) rejected maximalist's risk-tiered/auto-approval-below-threshold design, and maximalist itself conceded in round 2. The synthesis holds that a configured policy is a standing instruction, not a per-transaction authorising act, and that PRE-R-04/PRE-R-10 require a distinct, accountable human approval event on every run. TGT-03 therefore remains a full human act for every proposal, strengthened only by better evidence-rich packet assembly (hitl_designer's and agentic_architect's refinement), never by removing the decision itself.

Council consensus that file formatting is mechanical and automatable but that transmission — the one irreversible act in the run — must retain an explicit human trigger (agentic_architect's non-negotiable, echoed by pragmatist, hitl_designer, finance_domain, emerging_economy; maximalist conceded this in round 2). The design adopts agentic_architect's pre-transmission fingerprint/verification gate against the approval-time snapshot, hard-blocking on any delta, plus an independent check before release (finance_domain's maker-checker, relaxed per emerging_economy's objection to mandating a second treasury headcount, into an independent-verifier equivalent) and emerging_economy's requirement that batch/manual channels be first-class, not a bolted-on fallback.

Although tagged unconstrained_by_design, accounting_standards and emerging_economy both established this step is functionally load-bearing because PRE-07/TGT-06 requires its output (PRE-R-06) and KB-11 determinability depends on a reconciled settlement event. The synthesis resolves the pragmatist/finance_domain/emerging_economy position (treasury-facing confirmation matching stays a distinct step owned by Treasury) against the agentic_architect/maximalist merged-pipeline design: agentic_architect itself conceded in round 2 to splitting the merged pipeline into two named, sequentially-loggable stages for traceability and segregation of duties. TGT-05 is retained as its own stage, channel-agnostic (API or manual reconciliation as co-equal paths per emerging_economy), with exceptions routed to a named Treasury-officer queue.

All members agree the two mandatory inputs (bank settlement confirmation, settlement-date exchange rate — PRE-R-06, PRE-R-07) must survive explicitly, and accounting_standards' non-negotiables (per-item, non-netted FX differences per KB-08; cutoff discipline per KB-03; no re-measurement of recognition basis per KB-01) are adopted in full. Routine posting is automated per maximalist/finance_domain/hitl_designer, but variance review, unmatched items and cutoff risk are retained with a GL accountant as an accountable exception owner, kept organisationally distinct from Treasury's TGT-05 per pragmatist/finance_domain's segregation-of-duties argument, which the synthesis adopts over agentic_architect's unified-exception-role alternative since no KB entry forecloses it either way and the council's majority favours retaining the distinction.

Unanimous agreement this step carries no accounting-standards or ordering weight (explicitly unconstrained) and is a pure, low-risk automation target. Fully system-generated and dispatched, sourced directly from the posting/clearing record per accounting_standards' condition that remittance content never diverge from subledger detail, with delivery failures routed to an AP-analyst exception queue (finance_domain, hitl_designer) and channel flexibility for vendors with uneven digital access (emerging_economy).

steps.actor: AP analyst (exception-queue owner) with automated selection/proposal agent
steps.description: An ERP-resident agent selects approved, matched invoices falling due under payment terms and groups them by vendor, currency and payment method into a payment proposal in a single automated pass, mirroring what modern ERPs already do under the hood. Items failing clean, rule-based selection — disputed holds, missing or stale vendor master data, FX items above a volatility threshold — are routed to a named AP-analyst exception queue rather than silently included or excluded. Every selection and grouping decision is logged with the rule that fired and the data snapshot it acted on, so the due-item list and proposal are fully reconstructable. The agent's write access is limited to the proposal object; it cannot create a payment instruction, and its system identity is structurally distinct from the approving signatory's. A documented manual/batch fallback exists where continuous ERP automation is not available.
steps.name: Automated due-item selection and proposal generation

steps.description: An automated screen runs duplicate-payment matching against payment history, blocked-vendor checks and vendor-bank-detail-change-log diffing against every proposal line, surfacing a flagged/unflagged partition together with the specific underlying evidence (the change-log entry, the matched prior payment, the blocklist hit) for each flag — never a bare verdict or aggregate count. The AP supervisor holds and documents a hold/release disposition on every flagged item. To guard against silent drift in the detection logic's false-negative rate, the supervisor also reviews a periodic random sample of unflagged lines rather than treating the clean path as self-certifying. This step precedes both payment approval and payment release.
steps.name: Proposal review with automated screening and supervisory disposition

steps.description: An authorised signatory, distinct from whoever operates the proposal-generation agent, performs a per-run, per-proposal human approval act on every payment run, with no value-based, risk-based, or pre-configured-policy auto-approval path for any item. The approval packet assembled for the signatory carries the full TGT-02 exception log and the specific evidence behind each resolved flag — not an aggregate count or a 'zero open exceptions' summary — together with the applicable delegation-of-authority limits, so the signatory exercises a genuine, attributable decision on the specific run in front of them rather than ratifying a standing instruction.
steps.name: Payment approval

steps.actor: Treasury officer (release trigger) with independent verifier
steps.description: The approved proposal is converted into a bank payment file by an automated agent. Immediately before transmission, a verification routine recomputes a fingerprint of vendor bank details and amounts and compares it against the snapshot captured at TGT-03 approval time; any delta — such as a bank-detail change landing in the window between approval and release — hard-blocks transmission and escalates jointly to the AP supervisor and Treasury officer, and cannot be overridden by the file-generation agent itself. Release to the bank requires an explicit trigger from a named Treasury officer, independently verified before transmission (by a second treasury officer where bench depth allows, or by an independent supervisor check of the file against the approved proposal where it does not). No agent may trigger transmission autonomously. Batch/manual file-transfer channels (e.g., signed SFTP upload) remain a first-class, documented mechanism alongside API-based transmission, not a fallback bolted on after the fact.
steps.name: Payment file generation and release with pre-transmission verification gate

steps.description: Bank settlement confirmations are ingested — via API/SWIFT feed where available, or via manual bank-statement reconciliation as an equally first-class channel where continuous connectivity is not available — and matched to the transmitted payment file by reference, producing a distinct, logged, reconcilable settlement-confirmation artifact that anchors posting. Unmatched items, partial settlements, returns and rejects are routed to a named Treasury-officer exception queue, and any return or rejection flows back to re-open the relevant AP open item rather than disappearing. This function remains Treasury-owned and distinct from GL posting so that a suspicious or unmatched settlement is never posted by the same role that also controls the bank-facing side.
steps.name: Bank settlement confirmation matching

steps.description: Settled payments are posted against the logged bank settlement confirmation and the settlement-date exchange rate — sourced from a documented, defensible reference rate — clearing open items in the AP subledger and recording cash in the GL. Exchange differences are computed and posted explicitly and individually, item by item, never netted into an aggregate plug. Routine postings within tolerance are automated; settlement differences outside a defined tolerance band, unmatched confirmations, or manually-forced postings are routed to the GL accountant for investigation and sign-off before finalisation. A cutoff control (subledger lock or equivalent) ensures that any lag between bank execution and automated posting does not let settlements drift across a reporting-period boundary unacknowledged. This step settles previously recognised liabilities; it does not re-open or re-measure the original recognition basis beyond the FX difference contemplated at settlement.
steps.name: Posting and clearing

steps.description: Remittance advice is system-generated and dispatched directly from the TGT-06 posting/clearing record as soon as settlement is posted, so remittance content is sourced from, and can never diverge from, the subledger clearing detail. Delivery channel is not assumed to be email/portal-only; batch-file delivery, vendor-bank channel delivery or other appropriate channels remain valid given uneven digital access among vendors. Delivery failures and vendor disputes about what a remittance covered are routed to an AP-analyst exception queue.
steps.name: Remittance advice to vendors
